I can proudly say that my social anxiety has lessened to almost non existant after a lot of working on myself. But I still say um a lot.

In speech class we were trained to "pause" everytime you feel the urge to uh or um. When we did our assignments the teacher would have someone in class volunteer to count your uh's and um's. The goal was to decrease with each speech. The final was giving a speech with none.
That's intense. I would have hated that class even though it is a beneficial skill to have.
I had study skills in 6th grade at my college prep. I'm not IN college and thinking about that class all the time. It definitely helped.
The thing is, this only works when there is one speaker, and an audience that will wait politely for them to continue. There's a reason we "um" in normal speech.

What's interesting is, a while ago in a linguistics paper, showed that the buffering sound: uh, um, ah, ato, etc. is understood in literally every language as 'hang on, there's more coming in a moment'
